Zenium extension runtime frame budget

StartLogin formComment boxVideoEnd

A long page served by the fixture server, scrolled under a finger with none, three and six extensions attached. Nothing here moves on its own.

1What the runtime adds to a frame

Scrolling a long page is the gesture a phone does most. The chrome must spend the frame on the page, and the extension runtime must spend nothing on it: content scripts run once per document, the bridge carries messages only when an extension asks for one, and rules are decided off the main thread before the request leaves.

Every section of this page holds a heading, prose with a few links, an emphasis or two and some inline code, so a content script that walks the tree has work to do at load and none to do on scroll. The sections are numbered so a screenshot tells how far the finger went.

2Content scripts at document start

Every section of this page holds a heading, prose with a few links, an emphasis or two and some inline code, so a content script that walks the tree has work to do at load and none to do on scroll. The sections are numbered so a screenshot tells how far the finger went.

A grammar checker attaches to editable fields, a password manager collects the forms, a dark mode reads the colours of every image, and an ad blocker matches the cosmetic filters of the site. All of that is load-time work. What shows in the frames of a scroll is whatever any of them does per scroll event or per mutation, and what the runtime does to carry it.

3The bridge under a finger

A grammar checker attaches to editable fields, a password manager collects the forms, a dark mode reads the colours of every image, and an ad blocker matches the cosmetic filters of the site. All of that is load-time work. What shows in the frames of a scroll is whatever any of them does per scroll event or per mutation, and what the runtime does to carry it.

The recipe measured here is the emulator on a software GPU: frame times compare against the same scroll with no extension attached, never against a device. The numbers to hold are the ratios, the janky share above the baseline and the renderer main thread time per frame in the trace.

5Declarative rules on the request path

Links: first section, the middle, the last line. Words that a spell checker underlines: recieve, occurence, seperate. Words it should not: Zenium, WebView, Chromium.

Nothing on this page is fetched from the network beyond the runner that serves it: the images are one SVG asked for under many names so every one of them is a request the engine decides, and the clip is the fixture server’s own.

  • Frames: every frame HWUI drew during the scene.
  • Janky share: the frames over the deadline, as a share.
  • p50, p95, p99: the frame time percentiles.
  • The long stage: where the slowest frames spent their time.
  • Bridge messages per second: what the runtime moved meanwhile.
